title: Eliminate legacy bucket overlap and duplicate credit lines in billing exports
creator: Asha Menon
description: Summary: Customers have reported invoice mismatches where rate-limit credit lines are duplicated and usage is attributed to overlapping billing buckets. Root cause analysis found two independent issues: (1) the legacy meter-service used a localtime-based bucketing window for some tenants created before 2024-01-01, which produced overlapping usage buckets when customers changed org timezone or during DST transitions; (2) the billing-export transform lacks idempotent collapsing for credit events, causing duplicate credit rows in Stripe exports and subsequent NetSuite invoices when re-run or retried. This ticket fixes both the canonical bucketing logic and the export pipeline's dedup/collapse semantics, plus a safe backfill and reconciliation path for affected invoices.
acceptance_criteria: Metering buckets are computed in canonical UTC floor windows for all tenants (legacy flag removed) and unit tests cover DST/timezone edgecases
Billing export deduplication added: repeated credit events for the same credit_token within an invoice window are collapsed to a single line item in Stripe/NetSuite exports
Backfill script reprocesses affected billing windows for customers with duplicate credits from 2025-10-01 to present and produces reconciliation report
No new duplicate credit line items appear in a 7-day canary cohort (sample of 200 customers) after rollout
Acceptance dashboards show invoice line count deltas and credit-amount variance within expected thresholds (<=0.1% of customers flagged)
Manual review checklist for >$5k corrections documented and run for first 50 high-value accounts
implementation_plan: Add migration to meter-service to normalize legacy tenants: change bucketing to UTC-flooring and mark legacy_flag=false (atomic, reversible via feature flag)
Modify billing-export pipeline (export-transform service) to use credit_token idempotency key and collapse duplicates within invoice window; add deterministic sort for merging line items
Introduce idempotent export markers (export_run_id) to Stripe/NetSuite exports to prevent double-apply when retries occur
Write SQL-based backfill that identifies invoices with duplicate credit_token for same invoice_id, creates a staging reconciliation table and emits proposed adjustments
Create backfill runner that runs in controlled batches with checkpointing and dry-run mode; produce reconciliation CSVs for finance review
Canary rollout: enable feature flag for export dedup and UTC bucketing for 200 customers for 7 days; monitor dashboards and error rates
Full rollout with phased backfill: first reprocess low-value invoices automatically, escalate high-value (> $5k) to manual review
Post-migration: remove legacy_flag and older code paths after 30 days of stable operation
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Backfill could create invoice adjustments that confuse customers or duplicate corrections if re-run. Mitigation: backfill is idempotent via reconciliation table and export_run_id; finance requires manual approval for >$5k adjustments
Risk: Small timing window where live exports may interleave with backfill leading to transient duplicates. Mitigation: exports check export_run_id and lock invoice windows during backfill batches

Risk: Timezone normalization may change historic usage attribution visible in dashboards. Mitigation: only normalize for billing buckets (not raw usage events) and provide an audit trail; publish Confluence note and email impacted customers selected for manual review
monitoring_and_rollout_metrics: Metric: duplicate_credit_lines_per_1000_invoices (target: drop to 0 within canary)
Metric: net_revenue_adjustment_sum_daily (finance dashboard for backfill corrections)
SLO: export pipeline % success (target >= 99.9% during rollout)
